encounters.deskAlert: Whip Fenrir Fang is leaning casually against your office doorframe.

n1.text: Welcome to Washington, Barnaby! Adorable bow tie. Quick orientation: our $40B National School Infrastructure Grant Act hits the House floor shortly. Parents and contractors want federal grant money flowing home, and Leadership needs a crisp AYE—don't get squeamish over the pay-for attachment.

choices.label: You got it, Whip. Put me down for an AYE.
I read every federal bill before committing—check back on the floor.
I answer to Maple Creek, not your whip sheet.

n2_deal.text: Good boy! Keep your word on the floor and Leadership will owe you a Favor—worth 12 House seats when you bring your Flagship Bill to the floor. Just... don't double-cross my clipboard.

choices.label: Back to the Desk

n2_hedge.text: Heh. Careful, rookie. If your Caucus standing sinks into Backbench Exile, Leadership will actively pull seats off your Flagship hemicycle. I'll be watching the tally board.

choices.label: Back to the Desk

n2_refuse.text: Oh, an idealist! Charming. Let's see how you reach 51 seats on your Flagship Bill without Leadership's help.

choices.label: Back to the Desk

encounters.deskAlert: An embossed silk envelope slid under your door—Vesper Viper requests two minutes.

n1.text: Good morning, Representative Barker. Vesper Viper, Senior Counsel on K-Street. Today's Federal Clean Waterways Act imposes costly national compliance mandates on every riverside mill and small manufacturer—including back in Maple Creek. Vote NAY, and your reelection War Chest will stay comfortably full.

choices.label: Promise a NAY—campaigns and small workshops both need breathing room.
I'll 'review the federal economic impact study' first.
Show yourself out, Viper. Families deserve clean national rivers and toll-free federal crossings.

n2_deal.text: Exquisite pragmatism. Keep your promise on the floor and consider me a loyal supporter. Break it, and my clients have remarkably long memories.

choices.label: Back to the Desk

n2_hedge.text: Ah—fluent Capitolese for 'sharpen your offer.' Just remember, Barnaby: running on fumes when primary season starts is fatal.

choices.label: Back to the Desk

n2_refuse.text: How delightfully noble! Best of luck answering prime-time attack ads with an empty War Chest.

choices.label: Back to the Desk

encounters.deskAlert: Rep. Wilbur Troughman is flagging you down outside the Members' Dining Room.

n1.text: Barnaby! My favorite freshman! Today's National Freight Rail Corridor Act puts a regional federal depot right near Maple Creek—150 local jobs—AND carries a modest federal concrete earmark for my state. Back it with an AYE, and I'll owe you 10 Appropriations seats whenever you call your Flagship Bill!

choices.label: Main Street needs those rail jobs—promise AYE. Remember me on my Flagship Bill, Wilbur.
Wait—what's the catch for residential neighborhoods along the rail corridor?
Keep your $380M earmark off national transit bills.

n2_ask.text: Oh, just federal eminent-domain and freight-noise waivers along the tracks! Retirees might grumble about midnight train horns, sure—but your Main Street merchants will build you a statue! Are you in?

choices.label: Fine. Promise AYE—just deliver on my Flagship Bill.
No deal, Wilbur. I'll decide on the floor.

n2_deal.text: Now THAT is how Washington coalitions get built! Don't get cold paws on the floor!

choices.label: Back to the Desk

n2_refuse.text: Hmph! Check with Sal Viper before you kill 150 federal rail jobs, kid—you might be surprised who's mad at you!

choices.label: Back to the Desk

encounters.deskAlert: URGENT: Someone you double-crossed on a floor promise is pounding on your door!

n1.text: YOU SHOOK MY HAND, PROMISED YOUR VOTE, AND THEN DOUBLE-CROSSED ME ON THE FLOOR! Did you think nobody reads the congressional roll call in Washington, Barker?!

choices.label: I'm sorry—I read the attachment at the last second and balked.
Your attachment hurt Maple Creek—I stand by my vote.
Calm down—I'll back today's Federal Postal bill to make it right.

n2_apologize.text: Word travels faster than gossip on Capitol Hill. Don't expect favors until your handshake actually means something.

choices.label: Back to the Desk

n2_defiant.text: Bold bark for a freshman with split polls. Watch your flank when primary season rolls around.

choices.label: Back to the Desk

n2_promise_again.text: One last chance, rookie. Burn us twice and we'll fly a polished primary challenger straight into your district.

choices.label: Back to the Desk

encounters.deskAlert: Chairwoman Beatrice Kodiak requests a quiet word in your office.

n1.text: Representative Barker. I have chaired the House Rules Committee for thirty years. Today's Federal Postal Restructuring Act arrives with heavy black redactions. Online shops love cheaper federal parcel rates, yet rural seniors nationwide may pay dearly for what sits beneath that ink.

choices.label: Thank you, Chairwoman. I intend to uncover every blacked-out line.
If I kill it, will you whip seats for my Flagship Bill?

n2_respect.text: Good. Read what others try to obscure, and you may learn that institutional respect carries more weight than loud slogans.

choices.label: Back to the Desk

n2_transactional.text: Do not haggle with the Rules Chair, young pup. Earn respect first; favors follow merit.

choices.label: Back to the Desk

encounters.deskAlert: Whip Fenrir Fang is blocking the elevator with a 1,204-page federal omnibus binder.

n1.text: Listen closely, Barker. Today's Federal Budget Omnibus bundles SBA small-business disaster loans, rural hospital grants, and 'budget offsets' into one take-it-or-leave-it vote. Stamp AYE and earn a 12-seat Leadership Favor for your Flagship Bill. Stamp NAY and we'll tell every shop and retiree back home you blocked disaster aid.

choices.label: Fine—I'll vote AYE. Keep my Caucus standing safe.
What exactly is buried on Page 1,204, Fenrir?
Forcing Congress to trade federal school grants against disaster loans is broken.

n2_cave.text: Sensible pup. Heads up—Mags Magpie is camped outside the chamber doors with a six-second microphone.

choices.label: Back to the Desk

n2_probe.text: Merely routine 'Title I spending restraint and congressional member allowances.' Flip all three pages on the floor—and brace for the press ambush!

choices.label: Back to the Desk

n2_stand.text: Save the civics speech for Mags Magpie—she's waiting right outside the chamber doors!

choices.label: Back to the Desk

encounters.deskAlert: Rep. Wilbur Troughman pops in about H.R. 512—and checks how your Flagship seat count is looking!

n1.text: Morning, Barnaby! Hope you're watching that House hemicycle on your MY BILL folder—you can bring your Flagship Bill to the floor any week from Week 4 through Week 8! Meanwhile, today's Rural Telehealth & Copay bill is up. Pharma wants a quiet AYE—and Seniors love lower copays—even if small shops grumble about the 2% payroll offset.

choices.label: Lower copays for seniors is a winner—put me down for an AYE.
I'll inspect Amendment #8C on the floor before promising anything.
A 12-year patent monopoly AND a payroll tax on small shops? No thanks.

n2_deal.text: Smart operator! Viper's clients will remember that—and don't forget to check your Flagship hemicycle before Week 8 closes!

choices.label: Back to the Desk

n2_hedge.text: Suit yourself, kid. Just remember—every roll-call vote moves minor caucus reps onto or off your own Flagship Bill!

choices.label: Back to the Desk

n2_refuse.text: Careful, pup—Retirees back home will hear you voted against prescription copay caps!

choices.label: Back to the Desk

encounters.deskAlert: BREAKING: A dazzlingly polished Fox is filming a national-donor campaign ad outside your door!

n1.text: Hey there, Barnaby! Sterling Foxworth—your brand-new Primary Challenger! No hard feelings, pal. My hair tested at 94% favorability, and if your War Chest is running dry, my billboards are going to chew through Maple Creek support every single week from here to Election Day!

choices.label: Maple Creek voters see straight through a focus-grouped campaign.
Check my War Chest, Sterling—I can match your ad buys.
Wait—who's paying for all those glossy billboards along Highway 9?!

n2_grassroots.text: Ooh, love the hometown pluck! Now go untangle four nested negatives on H.R. 615 while my cameras roll!

choices.label: Back to the Desk

n2_money.text: Whoa, look at the rookie flexing donor cash! My ad editors are gonna love that clip.

choices.label: Back to the Desk

n2_ask.text: A totally independent national committee called 'Citizens for Fresh Leadership.' See you on the ballot, Barnaby!

choices.label: Back to the Desk

encounters.deskAlert: Vesper Viper is waiting with a 'federal campaign ethics bill'—and an ad-war lifeline.

n1.text: Foxworth's billboards are brutal, aren't they, Barnaby? If your War Chest is running dry, today's Federal Election Ethics Act is your lifeline. Ignore the redacted FEC rules, stamp AYE, and my K-Street donors will fund your television counter-blitz overnight.

choices.label: I can't fight Foxworth broke. Promise AYE.
A federal 'ethics' bill with blacked-out clauses? I'll scrub it myself.

n2_deal.text: Spoken like a survivor! Keep your word and the airwaves will be yours.

choices.label: Back to the Desk

n2_refuse.text: Still principled while Foxworth owns every radio commercial back home? Bold strategy.

choices.label: Back to the Desk

encounters.deskAlert: Chairwoman Kodiak stands at your door holding a wax-sealed endorsement letter.

n1.text: That glossy challenger is turning your race into a circus, Barker. I am prepared to endorse your reelection—worth a decisive swing on Election Night. Today's Federal Highway Trust Fund Omnibus holds my own 72-Hour Reading Rule, yet somebody hid 75-year no-bid federal contracts on Page 3. Expose it and vote NAY—even if freight shippers groan—and the Kodiak seal is yours.

choices.label: You have my word, Chairwoman. I'll block the rigged Page 3.
Regional freight needs Highway 9 rebuilt—I can't pledge a NAY until I read it.

n2_pledge.text: Well spoken. Scrub the ink, hold the line, and brace for Mags Magpie in the hallway.

choices.label: Back to the Desk

n2_honest.text: Candor is rare on Capitol Hill. Inspect Page 3 on the floor; if you vote NAY to strip the no-bid contracts, my endorsement will still be yours.

choices.label: Back to the Desk

encounters.deskAlert: ELECTION EVE: Shutdown deadline at midnight—and three urgent closing-night offers arrive!

n1.text: Barnaby! Polls open at sunrise tomorrow! Congress is racing a midnight Government Shutdown vote, and every group is knocking with a closing pitch. Check Toby's Staffer Report to see where you're weakest—how are you closing your campaign?

choices.label: Fly Back for a Midnight Maple Creek Rally (+11 all 3 hometown blocs, -10 Funds)
Accept Viper's Last-Minute National Ad Blitz (+22 Funds, -9 all 3 blocs)
Sign Whip Fang's Final Caucus Loyalty Pledge (+19 Party, -7 all 3 blocs)

n2_grassroots.text: Sal Viper's bringing coffee, Mrs. Lupine's organizing carpools, and Boarwell is handing out voter guides! Now go handle the midnight Shutdown Resolution!

choices.label: To the Final Floor Vote!

n2_snake.text: Barnaby... a velvet-briefcase check at 11 PM on Election Eve? Don't be surprised if the Ethics Board takes an interest.

choices.label: To the Final Floor Vote!

n2_wolf.text: The Caucus turnout machine will roll at dawn—though folks back in Maple Creek will notice whose leash you signed.

choices.label: To the Final Floor Vote!

promptByVote.aye: FLASH! Mags Magpie, Capitol Gazette! Rep. Barker, you just froze federal Title I school grants and TRIPLED congressional member allowances! How do you face parents back home?!
promptByVote.nay: FLASH! Mags Magpie, Capitol Gazette! Whip Fang says you just voted AGAINST federal SBA disaster loans and rural senior heating aid! Any comment?!
promptByVote.abstain: FLASH! Mags Magpie, Capitol Gazette! You seriously ABSTAINED on a 1,204-page federal spending bill?! Were you napping at your desk?!

choices.label: "Page 1,204 froze federal school grants to triple Capitol perks—pass clean disaster aid separately!"
choices.successText: Mags lowers her notepad: 'Whoa—sharp quote. Rewriting the morning front page!'
choices.failText: Mags cackles: 'YOU VOTED AYE ON IT, BARKER! That's going in 72-point bold!'
choices.flubText: You blink hard into the flash bulb and stammer through the sentence—Mags catches the awkward pause on tape!
choices.successHeadline: BARKER TO PRESS: "PASS CLEAN DISASTER AID WITHOUT TRIPLE CAPITOL PERKS!"
choices.successSubhead: Rep. Barker's razor-sharp hallway counterpunch turns public heat back onto omnibus leadership.
choices.failHeadline: FACT-CHECK FIASCO! BARKER BLASTS PAGE 1,204—AFTER VOTING 'AYE' ON IT!
choices.failSubhead: "Pass clean aid separately!" Barker shouted, momentarily forgetting he had just rubber-stamped the 1,204-page bill.
choices.flubHeadline: FLASH-BLINDED! BARKER STAMMERS ON LIVE MIC TRYING TO EXPLAIN OMNIBUS VOTE!
choices.flubSubhead: A shaky delivery outside the chamber turns Barker's defense of school grants into an awkward viral clip.

choices.label: "Small businesses and seniors needed emergency federal aid tonight—I'll file a standalone school bill Monday!"
choices.successText: Mags squints: 'Slick framing. Fine—I'll run a photo of Main Street Bakery instead.'
choices.failText: Mags grins: 'You voted NAY and you're taking credit for disaster aid? Instant meme!'
choices.flubText: Your voice cracks right as the flash bulb pops—Mags gets a hilarious mid-sneeze snapshot!
choices.successHeadline: BARKER VOWS MONDAY SCHOOL FIX: "MAIN STREET & SENIORS NEEDED AID TONIGHT!"
choices.successSubhead: Poised under hallway cameras, Barker softens the omnibus backlash by pledging standalone Title I relief.
choices.failHeadline: WAIT—WHAT?! BARKER CLAIMS CREDIT FOR DISASTER AID HE JUST VOTED DOWN!
choices.failSubhead: Reporters burst out laughing as Barker vows to fix a bill he had stamped NAY moments earlier.
choices.flubHeadline: VOICE CRACK HEARD 'ROUND THE HILL! BARKER FUMBLES OMNIBUS DEFENSE ON CAMERA!
choices.flubSubhead: Barker promised a Monday school bill, though viewers mostly replayed his squeaky microphone sneeze.

choices.label: "Look behind you—Rep. Troughman dropped his fountain pen!" (Bolt down the stairs)
choices.successText: Mags actually turns! You escape the hallway with only a mildly teasing cartoon.
choices.failText: Mags snaps a mid-air blur of your flapping bow tie. Instant viral front page.
choices.flubText: You trip over a marble potted plant mid-sprint as Mags's flash fires three times!
choices.successHeadline: CAPITOL ESCAPE ARTIST: BARKER DODGES PRESS CORPS WITH FOUNTAIN-PEN FAKEOUT!
choices.successSubhead: Mags Magpie admits the freshman pulled off 'a textbook stairwell vanish' after abstaining.
choices.failHeadline: FLAPPING BOW TIE! BARKER LITERALLY SPRINTS AWAY FROM OMNIBUS QUESTIONS!
choices.failSubhead: "Look, a fountain pen!" yelled the freshman before vanishing down the marble stairs in a viral blur.
choices.flubHeadline: POTTED-PLANT TUMBLE! BARKER TRIPS MID-ESCAPE FROM PRESS GALLERY!
choices.flubSubhead: The Capitol Gazette prints a three-frame photo sequence of Barker's hallway somersault.

pressAmbushes.timeoutHeadline: FROZEN PUP! BARKER STARES SPEECHLESS INTO FLASH CAMERA!

promptByVote.aye: FLASH! Rep. Barker! You just handed out 75-YEAR NO-BID FEDERAL CONTRACTS with zero Inspector General audits! Was Highway 9 worth selling the treasury?!
promptByVote.nay: FLASH! Sterling Foxworth is already airing ads claiming you blocked emergency federal Highway Trust Fund repairs! Your response?!
promptByVote.abstain: FLASH! Election is next week and you ABSTAINED on the Federal Highway Trust Fund! Who are you trying to please?!

choices.label: "I blocked 75-year no-bid corruption—pass a clean standalone Highway Trust Fund bill right now!"
choices.successText: Mags whistles: 'Kodiak's backing that line too! Foxworth's attack ad just fell flat!'
choices.failText: Mags flashes her bulb: 'You literally just voted AYE for those no-bid contracts! Front page!'
choices.flubText: You cough into the microphone right on the word 'corruption'—Foxworth's ad editors are grinning!
choices.successHeadline: BARKER TO FOXWORTH: "I BLOCKED 75-YEAR NO-BID CORRUPTION—PASS CLEAN BRIDGES!"
choices.successSubhead: Backed by Chairwoman Kodiak, Barker's poised hallway quote blunts Foxworth's Highway 9 attack blitz.
choices.failHeadline: BUSTED ON TAPE! BARKER DENOUNCES NO-BID CONTRACTS MINUTES AFTER VOTING 'AYE'!
choices.failSubhead: "I blocked corruption!" insisted Barker as Mags Magpie held up the official House roll-call sheet.
choices.flubHeadline: COUGHING FIT AT THE MIC! BARKER STUMBLES DEFENDING HIGHWAY 9 VOTE!
choices.flubSubhead: A rattled delivery weakens Barker's rebuttal just as Foxworth buys extra evening airtime.

choices.label: "Freight routes needed federal bridge aid tonight—I'll demand Inspector General audits Monday!"
choices.successText: Mags shrugs: 'Smooth pivot. Half the town will give you the benefit of the doubt.'
choices.failText: Mags laughs: 'Auditing a bill you just voted down?! Classic Capitol word salad!'
choices.flubText: You squint blindly at the flash and mumble 'Inspector General... uh... Tuesday?'
choices.successHeadline: BARKER DEFENDS HIGHWAY VOTE: "FREIGHT NEEDED BRIDGES—AUDITS COMING MONDAY!"
choices.successSubhead: Cool under camera lights, Barker pitches his omnibus AYE as urgent relief for Main Street haulers.
choices.failHeadline: WORD SALAD! BARKER VOWS TO AUDIT A HIGHWAY BILL HE JUST KILLED!
choices.failSubhead: Even Foxworth looked genuinely confused as Barker demanded oversight on legislation that failed.
choices.flubHeadline: "INSPECTOR... TUESDAY?" BARKER RATTLES UNDER HALLWAY FLASH BULBS!
choices.flubSubhead: A nervous stammer leaves Maple Creek wondering whether those promised audits will ever arrive.

choices.label: "No comment—see you at the ballot box, Mags!"
choices.failText: Mags grins wickedly: 'In print, No Comment ALWAYS reads like a guilty plea!'
choices.flubText: You accidentally walk into the broom closet while saying 'See you at the ballot box!'
choices.successHeadline: BARKER STAYS MUM ON HIGHWAY OMNIBUS: "SEE YOU AT THE BALLOT BOX!"
choices.successSubhead: Refusing to engage Mags Magpie leaves pundits filling in the blanks ahead of Election Eve.
choices.failHeadline: "NO COMMENT!" BARKER BRUSHES PAST REPORTERS AFTER HIGHWAY SHOWDOWN!
choices.failSubhead: Mags Magpie notes in print that 'No Comment' rarely polls well one week before Election Day.
choices.flubHeadline: BROOM-CLOSET EXIT! BARKER SAYS 'NO COMMENT' AND WALKS INTO JANITOR'S SUPPLY ROOM!
choices.flubSubhead: A six-second hallway clip of Barker emerging with a mop bucket dominates evening news.
